description: Labelled interviewer utterances. Each example carries a coarse `intent` (what kind of answer is required) and a fine `topic` (subject matter). Two classifiers are trained from this file; it doubles as the intent benchmark.

classes.self_introduction: Requests to summarise the candidate's background and career story.
classes.past_experience: Requests for a concrete past experience; answered with a STAR story.
classes.self_assessment: Requests for the candidate's strengths or weaknesses.
classes.people: Questions about conflict, collaboration, mentoring and leadership.
classes.hypothetical: Hypothetical 'what would you do if' questions.
classes.knowledge: Requests to explain a technical concept or compare approaches.
classes.design: Requests to architect or scale a system.
classes.coding: Requests to write, complete or read code.
classes.troubleshooting: Questions about why a system or piece of code misbehaves.
classes.background: Questions about hands-on experience, education or self-directed learning.
classes.motivation: Questions about why the candidate wants this role or company.
classes.goals: Questions about long term career direction.
classes.culture: Questions about values, work style and environment preferences.
classes.measurement: Questions about metrics, success criteria or impact.
classes.logistics: Salary, equity, notice period, availability and interview logistics.

topics.technical_concept: Languages, frameworks, data structures and theory.
topics.architecture: System design, scaling and distributed systems.
topics.collaboration: Working with peers, stakeholders and cross-functional partners.
topics.judgement: Trade-off reasoning and hypothetical decision making.
topics.learning: Education, courses and self-directed skill building.
topics.self: The candidate's own strengths, weaknesses and story.
topics.company: The employer, its product and the candidate's motivation.
topics.career: Long term career direction and ambitions.
topics.culture: Work style, values and environment preferences.
